newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea says North able to overcome food crisis.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea says North able to overcome food crisis.

text.p: South Korea says the communist North can overcome its food shortage and the government in Pyongyang may be overstating the problem.
A statement by the Unification Ministry released late on Thursday contradicts U.N. warnings that North Korea faces famine with no food left by June 20.
"Given stockpiles secured from international organisations since last November, North Korea is forecast to tide over a food crisis," the ministry said.

"We cannot rule out the possibility that the North Korean government deliberately discloses some exaggerated data and statistics in order to continuously attract food aid from the international community."

Catherine Bertini, director of the Rome-based World Food Programme, told a news conference on Wednesday North Korea's food rationing system had nearly collapsed and people were facing starvation, with isolated deaths from malnutrition already being reported.
Wednesday's warning was the most serious in recent weeks on the food shortage, which has been caused by two years of flooding.
Five government distribution centres in North Korea had already run out of food and the remining five would do so by June 20, according to the WFP report.
But the Unification Ministry statement said the temporary halt in food distribution was likely due to inefficiency and poor transport infrastructure in the north.
The WFP has raised 144,464 tons of food donations in response to the floods. But Bertini said the country needed 1.8 million tons to avoid large-scale starvation.
U.S. grains giant Cargill Inc on Thursday said North Korea had cancelled a zinc-for-food barter deal, fanning concern over Pyongyang's ability to alleviate hunger.

Cargill was given permission by the Clinton administration to pursue sales of up to 500,000 tons of wheat and rice to North Korea, a rarely granted opportunity that came during a moment of warmer relations between the two nations.
